📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eight years after signing for Celtic and being compared to Henrik Larsson, Mohamed Bangura retired from football at the age of 29.

Industry observers note that born in Kambia in Sierra Leone, Bangura joined FC Kallon, one of the top clubs in his home country, at a young age. Impressing for the Freetown-based club, he made the switch to Europe, playing for two different Swedish sides before earning his big move to Celtic in 2011.

He'd go on to make just 16 appearances for the Scottish giants, before joining Istanbul Basksehir in 2014 after having had his contract at Celtic Park terminated by mutual consent.

After leaving Turkey, he spent time in China and back in Sweden, before eventually hanging up his boots in 2019 after failing to find a new club following his release from Superettan side Dalkurd.

An extremely prolific number nine in Sierra Leone's top flight for Kallon, several clubs across Europe were keeping tabs on Bangura's development towards the end of the 2000s. Swedish third division side IFK Varnamo were able to negotiate a short-term loan with Kallon for the young striker, and in March 2010, he made his way to Scandinavia to commence his career in Europe.

In a recent development, after scoring 12 goals in 13 league appearances for Varnamo, Swedish giants AIK swept in and signed Bangura on a three-and-a-half-year deal. The Stockholm club fought off considerable interest from multiple potential suitors, with the player already garnering significant attention in Sweden at this point in his development.

Quick, intelligent and an expert finisher, there was a lot to like about the then 21-year-old. After just over 12 months at AIK, which saw 14 goals in 35 appearances, Celtic forked out £2.1 million to sign the Sierra Leonean. According to BBC Sport, Bangura had been recommended to the Glaswegian outfit by club legend Henrik Larsson, who had been closely observing the striker's progress in Sweden.

"I'm flattered that someone like Henrik Larsson would recommend me," Bangura said at the time.

According to recent reports, "I know all about what a great player he was for Celtic. I am delighted to be joining a club the size of Celtic.".

Naturally, Larsson's endorsement led many to tip Bangura to emulate the legendary forward's achievements at Celtic Park. The Swede scored 242 goals in 313 appearances for Celtic between 1997 and 2004, and the club's supporters were yearning for a similarly productive number nine to replicate these feats.

Sources indicate that the pressure this created clearly got to Bangura, who didn't come remotely close to being Larsson's long-term successor. After failing to find the back of the net early on, manager Neil Lennon started favouring strikers Gary Hooper, Anthony Stokes and Georgios Samaras. This fall in the pecking order, combined with a serious knee injury, saw the young centre-forward finish his debut season in Scotland with no goals in just 15 appearances.

It has been revealed that the following season, after finding himself on the periphery of Lennon's squad, he returned to AIK on loan. This was the first of two loan spells back in the Scandinavian nation, as he'd later join Elfsborg for a short period, before Celtic opted to terminate his contract in 2014, leaving him searching for a new employer.

In an attempt to resurrect his career, Bangura switched up his surroundings by moving south to Turkey in 2014. Signing for then second-tier side Istanbul Basaksehir, he struggled to break into the team, making just eight appearances before calling it quits in the historic pan-continental city.

It has been revealed that AIK granted him another lifeline shortly after, allowing their former striker to train with them as he looked for a latest team. After impressing during training, the Swedish outfit signed Bangura for a third time in December 2014. He enjoyed a brief renaissance during the 2015 Allsvenskan season, netting eight goals in 34 appearances.

Instead of remaining in Sweden, he once again opted for a new venture at the end of 2015, joining Chinese Super League side Dalian Yifang on a three-year deal. He only saw out a single year of this contract, with Dalian terminating his deal at the end of the first season after he'd failed to make an impact.

Recent findings suggest that once again, he was a free agent, and this time it took a lot longer to find a fresh place to ply his trade. Over a year after being forced out of Dalian, Bangura returned to Sweden again, but this time in the second tier. He signed for Dalkurd, but wasn't offered a new deal at the end of his solitary season with the Superettan side.

Bangura once again spent over 12 months searching for a latest home, but an offer never came. In January 2019, he gave up, calling time on his short-lived career, just eight years after being tipped for greatness at Celtic.

The Biancocelesti went into the break for international duty as Serie A leaders, and will be back on the field on Saturday afternoon when hosting struggling Lecce at the Stadio Olimpico.

Frattesi scored for Italy in the 3-1 Nations League victory over France at San Siro, but then pulled out of the squad for the trip to Belgium due to a muscular injury.

The midfielder underwent tests that confirmed a muscle strain, but the good news is that there were no lesions.

That means he will be monitored over the next few days, and could well be available against Lecce on Saturday.

Zaccagni was ruled out of the Italy squad entirely due to a left quadricep injury, and the scan showed improvement in the condition, so over the next few days could be brought back into full training.

As for Nuno Tavares, he limped off with an injury in the game with Napoli, and is continuing the scheduled physiotherapy programme, as Lazio still expect to be without him for three weeks.

There may be more than six weeks until the January transfer window opens, but Manchester United are already considering how they can back upcoming manager Mauricio Pochettino in the market.

Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick's successor at Man United on Friday, and he will officially leave his role as the United States manager after they play Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning, UK time.

The 54-year-old will then travel to Manchester, where he will only have a couple of days to prepare for his bow against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

It's a difficult fixture for a club who have only won one of their 10 Premier League matches this term, which has left them in the relegation zone as we approach December.

A big improvement is needed on the pitch and Pochettino must find that tune out of the players he has at his disposal, before the club can potentially make additions in January.

Fabrizio Romano has already confirmed that there will be at least one upcoming signing in the New Year, and potentially two or three, with centre-back and striker the two priority positions.

According to talkSPORT reporter Alex Crook, the Red Devils are interested in Fulham duo Calvin Bassey and Antonee Robinson, while Folarin Balogun is a potential target having narrowly missed out on joining Premier League rivals Everton on deadline day in the summer.

Robinson and Balogun have both worked under Pochettino for the USMNT, while Bassey could kill two birds with one stone for the Red Devils given he can play both left-sided centre-back and left-back, amid the possibility that both Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw could leave Old Trafford in 2027.

One other player that is being looked at, according to Crook, is Brentford captain Nathan Collins.

Pochettino's Tottenham team was built around a strong leadership team put in place for the Argentine, and it allowed them to thrive.

Goalkeeper Hugo Lloris was club captain for much of the 54-year-old manager's time at Spurs, but he was backed up by Harry Kane and Jan Vertonghen at the time.

Pochettino is inheriting some good leaders on paper at Old Trafford, including captain Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire, while the likes of Luke Shaw, Diogo Dalot, Youri Tielemans and Lisandro Martinez offer plenty of experience.

Nathan Collins is unlikely to walk into the Theatre of Dreams and become captain, but the fact that he is at the moment the skipper of both Brentford and the Republic of Ireland demonstrates what an vital addition to the dressing room he would be.

And that is just one of Collins' strengths, given he has established himself as one of the best in his position in the Premier League in recent seasons.

The Irishman, described as 'very talented' by Thomas Frank when he joined the Bees, stands at 6ft 5in tall and is known for his aerial prowess when it comes to winning headed duels, while he has strong tackling and clearance statistics for the Bees.

Brentford are also known to play out from the back, and that is something that Collins has proven he is more than capable of doing, which will suit Pochettino down to the ground.

That quality to make progressive passes from defence is increasingly important in the modern game, and the 25-year-old is capable of that and much more, even if he hasn't been able to show it too much this season because of injury.

Collins for Brentford (Premier League 2026-27).

One thing that could count against Collins is whether the Red Devils actually need a right-sided centre-back, given they already have Maguire, Leny Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt who prefer to play on the right.

There is a greater need for a left-sided player, given there are doubts over Martinez's future and Ayden Heaven is still yet to convince people that he should be a consistent starter.

In those terms, Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton might be a better addition, but Collins could cost a fraction of the price, especially given United and Brentford already have a working relationship after the Bryan Mbeumo deal in 2025.

Sources indicate that barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí, 19, has won Tuttosport's 2026 Golden Boy award for Europe's best under-21 player by a wide margin. The landslide puts a defender on top of a prize rarely won by one, and pushes Barcelona further clear as the club with the most winners.

This year’s vote was one-sided. No other candidate came close to the Barcelona defender.

It has been revealed that the margin reveals how settled the vote was. It also marks a rare win for a player in his position. Corriere dello Sport described him as only the second defender ever to win it. He succeeds PSG’s Désiré Doué, the 2025 winner.

Recent findings suggest that cubarsí now joins a club list that already featured Messi, Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Four of the five have come in the last six years. Pedri won in 2021, Gavi in 2022 and Lamine Yamal in 2024.

No player can win the award twice. Each Barcelona success therefore means a different young player reaching the top of the vote. The recent run points to a steady flow of talent into the first team.

According to recent reports, the award caps a strong year for the defender. He was a big part of Barcelona’s LaLiga and Super Cup wins. He was also named young player of the tournament as Spain won the World Cup. He started all eight of Spain’s games there. FIFA’s Young Player Award made him the first defender to receive it. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final. They kept seven clean sheets and conceded only once, in a 2-1 quarter-final win over Belgium. The Golden Boy arrives just weeks after he narrowly missed out on the Kopa Trophy.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that physicists used an algorithm to combine telescope measurements of a black hole in a different way from the original analysis.Credit: S.
  • The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration wowed the world in 2019 with the first picture ever taken of a black hole’s shadow.
  • To image black holes, the international EHT collaboration stitches together data it collects simultaneously from an array of ground-based radio telescopes that stretches across several continents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that physicists used an algorithm to combine telescope measurements of a black hole in a different way from the original analysis.Credit: S. Lai, N. Thyagarajan, O. I. Wong and F. Diakogiannis/CSIRO.

The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration wowed the world in 2019 with the first picture ever taken of a black hole’s shadow. Some researchers were unconvinced, arguing that the circular shape seen in that shot was an artefact of the team’s image-reconstruction techniques. Now, an independent group has reanalysed the EHT data, and its results, published on 11 November in Nature — including new images of the black hole — largely corroborate the original findings1.

To image black holes, the international EHT collaboration stitches together data it collects simultaneously from an array of ground-based radio telescopes that stretches across several continents. The reconstruction is extremely challenging, but in principle, the result is an image with the same level of detail, or resolution, that would be achieved with a single radio dish as wide as Earth.

Although blurry, the EHT shot of a supermassive black hole at the centre of the M87 galaxy was consistent with astrophysical models based on Albert Einstein’s general theory of relativity, which first predicted the existence of black holes. The image had a bright ring of roughly the correct radius, given what was known about the size of the black hole, with a darker disk at the centre.

It has been revealed that however, starting in 2022, Junichiro Makino, an astrophysicist at Kobe University in Japan, and his collaborators began questioning those conclusions2. By applying one of the data-analysis techniques the EHT collaboration had used, but with slightly different assumptions, Makino’s team obtained a different result. Their image demonstrates a glob of radio emissions rather than a ring.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, HARRISON, N.J. – Gotham FC head coach Juan Carlos Amoros criticized the field conditions at Sports Illustrated Stadium during the team's 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, a complaint that highlighted the infrastructure battles the league is grappling with during this season's playoffs.

It has been revealed that the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 in the build-up to Sunday's quarterfinal over the quality of the pitch, which appears to have been overworked in recent weeks. Gotham are a secondary tenant at the stadium, which is owned by Fresh Jersey's Hudson County and is primarily the home of the Red Bull New York. The MLS team played their regular season finale on Saturday evening, less than 24 hours before the 12:30 p.m. local time kickoff for the NWSL match. The stadium also hosted a rugby doubleheader the previous week, the scars of which were easy to spot over the course of Sunday's game.

"I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros remarked post-match. "I think at this level, in this kind of game, as a league, we should be having a better surface. Unfortunately, our football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn't but luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt and the game was what it was.".

Players on both teams complained of the playing conditions, including Gotham's Jaelin Howell, who worked her way back from an ankle concern in time for Sunday's match.

"Obviously it's pretty sandy out there and so a little unstable but I want to be able to give my all to the team and everything I got and so obviously can't think about that," Howell said. "The other team has to play on that, too, so we acknowledged it and we moved on and I think that our team managed it pretty well for the most part.".

The Reign's Jess Fishlock, a member of Seattle's squad since the inaugural NWSL season in 2013 who played the final match of her career, was more harsh in her assessment of the field.

"We performed so well for this group of players to come against a team like that at home on this field, which is atrocious, just saying it out loud," she said.

Her comments were echoed by Reign coach Laura Harvey, who has worked in and around the league since its inception.

Sources indicate that "Let's be real, there's no way a playoff game should be played on that shit," she told ESPN post-match. "I just can't believe they've allowed it. They knew it last week.".

Amoros said the field conditions ultimately impacted Gotham's ability to perform on Sunday, the NWSL Shield winners stringing together a performance he described as "not the best football match that you will ever see.".

In a recent development, "When you play on a pitch like that, you cannot be thinking of the next action or what you're gonna do once you get that ball," he mentioned. "You need to be looking at the ball because he can bounce at any given time. Plus, it just changes the whole dynamic of the game and it changes the dynamic of how we play. We adapted certain things. We adapted certain things on the game strategy. We had to be a bit more direct and certain situations but it definitely affected the way we played, yes.".

According to recent reports, gotham will conclude play at Sports Illustrated Stadium next Sunday at 3 p.m. local time in the NWSL semifinals against the Kansas City Current. The Red Bulls, who missed the MLS Cup playoffs for a second consecutive season, will host another match the night before, this time a friendly against Club America during the men's international break.

The pitch was an understandable obstacle for both teams but Gotham's struggles did not end there. The reigning champions, who are favored to win the championship for the third time in four seasons after winning the Shield, were second-best against the lowest-seeded team in the postseason. They benefitted from a fourth minute own goal from Jordyn Bugg, forced by standout Jaedyn Shaw, but were unable to actually assert any sort of dominance as the game progressed.

An unfortunate own goal and Gotham take the early lead ‼️NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/4LwZdfgLpx.

Gotham did not take a single shot on target over the course of the game, their six shots totaling just 0.17 expected goals. The Reign were not all that much better but momentum shifted their way in the second half, eventually racking up 11 shots and 0.54 expected goals. The visitors were stymied by Gotham defenders Tierna Davidson and Jess Carter, as well as 2024 goalkeeper of the year Ann-Katrin Berger.

Recent findings suggest that "She literally does it on a consistent basis," Shaw said about Berger. "It's crazy the kind of saves that she makes and I feel like she makes a worldly save at least once a game and I mean I think it's hard enough getting through a back line but to get through Ann is a whole other task and I think we're all really grateful to have her back there. I know I am as an attacker and I think we all just have full trust in her ability and she's just such an integral part of our team and the way that we like to play as well. Even from the goal, she's such a big piece of the way that we play and our style.".

AKB goes aerial to deny Mia Fishel a goal ✈️ pic.twitter.com/4lqMm623On.

Gotham's attack, though, had no such excuses. Midfielder Rose Lavelle exited the match at halftime as the coaching staff manages her minutes after dealing with a knock in recent weeks, her exit diluting their attack. Forward Sam Kerr, meanwhile, failed to register a single shot and took just 23 touches over the course of 90 minutes in an absent performance during an inconsistent return to the NWSL. The Australia international has scored just four goals in 18 games since joining Gotham in July, despite the fact that she has racked up 9.67 expected goals along the way.

Amoros credited the Reign for their ability to lock out Gotham's defense.

"I think they did a good job trying to stop certain situations," he mentioned. "I think that was the key. They did really well on the press. They were first and second in a lot of the duels and they obviously play short passes to then go diagonal, which obviously then is something difficult to defend and something that is a lot more doable than probably over a style of play. It's just different and we had complications with those situations to defend. At the same time, we defended them. I think that's the key.".

Shaw, who attempted to spearhead a lifeless Gotham attack, described a disjointed performance that the team will hope not to replicate the following week.

"I think we just need to be cleaner on the ball," Shaw noted. "Obviously, the surface doesn't really help but  just in general, I think we can be more comfortable on the ball, facing forward and just be clinical in our passes, which I think will help us get to the final third a little bit more with more quality chances on goal.".

How USMNT's Neil Pierre turned overseas loan into breakout season with Philadelphia Union

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • - Walking into Philadelphia Union training, there's one player who immediately sticks out due to towering over the rest of the team at center back: Neil Pierre.
  • Industry observers note that for an 19-year-old, just going to a new country is enough of an adjustment, and doing so while needing to break into a squad with ambition is quite a task, and Pierre did it while also learning a new position.
  • "He had the power, he had the drive, but he still needed the game smartness and the calmness of playing more senior minutes," Bjelland stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CHESTER, Pa. - Walking into Philadelphia Union training, there's one player who immediately sticks out due to towering over the rest of the team at center back: Neil Pierre. While a soft-spoken person in life, when you're 6-foot-7 on a soccer field, it's hard to miss him—even down to Chris Richards not believing it until he saw the Union defender in the United States Men's National Team camp. But height may also be the least interesting thing about Pierre's journey as he, like the Union, has taken MLS by storm since he returned from a loan spell in Denmark with Lyngby, where he helped the club gain promotion back to the Danish Superliga while getting a taste of what first-team soccer is like.

Industry observers note that for an 19-year-old, just going to a new country is enough of an adjustment, and doing so while needing to break into a squad with ambition is quite a task, and Pierre did it while also learning a new position. Because of the club setup, Pierre actually played right back, and explaining the setup to CBS Sports, one of his co-managers, Andreas Bjelland, wanted to find out how he could get the talented young defender into the squad.

"He had the power, he had the drive, but he still needed the game smartness and the calmness of playing more senior minutes," Bjelland stated. "And then he could get some extra minutes playing right back because we also had some really good center backs at that point playing really well. So it was a little bit of a mix of also getting him into play more and more.".

It has been revealed that this is a credit not only to Pierre's talent but also to his drive and versatility, as the Union man turned this into an excellent breakout where he scored four goals in 10 appearances while winning promotion and building confidence that he could do it as a soccer player along the way. Both the Union Academy and Pierre's own family helped set him up for success in a year that has become an absolute whirlwind. Following his success at Lyngby, alongside the Union falling to the bottom of the league, it was easy to question why Pierre wasn't with the team to start the season, but his time in Denmark was also formative. While it's easy to say that he should've been in Philadelphia from the start in hindsight, it was an important step for the Pierre that we see before us today.

Recent findings suggest that "In the beginning, it was definitely a little nerve-wracking and definitely nervous," Pierre remarked, reflecting during Philadelphia Union training. "I think I can give all credit to them; they've kind of taken me in as like a part of the family immediately, so I felt like there was no stress there, and then that translated to on the pitch and they gave me the confidence to play how I was supposed to play. And then also off the field, I think, because we would go to team outings all the time and get dinner together, so it was like a family on and off the field.".

According to recent reports, fast forward, and not only has Pierre been part of pulling the Union out of the bottom of the Eastern Conference, but he's also earned his first USMNT call-up and cap, and that was rapidly followed by a return call for Concacaf Nations League play, where the USMNT will face Haiti twice during this international window, but if not for his family, soccer may not have happened. When Pierre was younger, basketball was the first sport that he connected with, but he credits his brother Nelson Pierre (who is currently on loan from the Vancouver Whitecaps to the HFX Wanderers of the Canadian Premier League) and his father for why he is where he is now.

In a recent development, "If it wasn't for them, I would be playing basketball right now. 100%," Pierre remarked. "But I think through them it was like I saw the love they had for the sport, and like how much passion they had, so I was like obviously I wanted to follow in my dad and brother's footsteps and be able to have that passion for something. So then I followed them into soccer and it's been since ever since it's been like this.".

It has been revealed that considering his play for the Union this season, plenty are happy that Pierre made the decision to stick with soccer, but while his frame and closing speed do come with advantages, they also comes with things that he has to watch out for on the field, especially when defending against smaller players. Not only are they at times more agile than Pierre, but challenges that he makes can look worse too, and these are things that gaining more in-game experience has helped him prepare for, dealing with them and excelling.

He also has the benefit of playing not only for a coach that he knows from the Union youth ranks, but also for one who was a defender during his own professional career. In fact, Pierre has always had a defensive-minded head coach, even with the USMNT in Mauricio Pochettino, and that's something else that has been a benefit while he's getting his feet in the game.

According to recent reports, "Obviously, being young, playing with older players [my coaches have] pulled me aside, either showing me film or what they feel like they've seen, and it's obviously different hearing it from a coach that's played in your position and done it at the highest level," Pierre remarked. "Same with the national team with Poch, I think hearing stuff like that, it's like these guys have done it at a pro level for a long time, so they know what they're talking about.".

It has been revealed that add that to his natural skills, and you get a young defender that the Union can anchor the squad around. Before even getting into his goals, his closing speed and positioning are able to anchor a defense that has allowed the third-fewest goals in MLS since the World Cup, with only 21. They may not have risen to first in the Eastern Conference, but when the squad only had seven points prior to the World Cup and has picked up 40 after it so far, the impact that Pierre and the rest of the squad have had to push their way into the playoffs has been quite remarkable. You can also see why Lyngby wanted to keep him for their season in the Danish top flight, but when the Union had a chance at a starting spot, it was hard to allow Pierre to go back on loan when he could help the first team.

"We can be super aggressive because Neil is comfortable in one-on-one situations. If it's a direct ball, he wins; he eats all of these. If it's open space that he has to defend, physically, he can deal with that, and he's also a good defender," Philly's interim coach, Ryan Richter, said about how Pierre's play impacts his squad. "The way he puts out so many fires allows us to be aggressive higher up the field, because we know when they play the ball long that we have someone who cleans this up almost every time.".

Defenders usually peak later than attackers in soccer, so it's impressive that Pierre is catching on so swiftly, but given his path of getting into first-team soccer and also being with the coach who he came up through the academy with, it's a good spot for Pierre to succeed and grow before his next step likely takes him back to Europe.

It has been revealed that "I think as a person, he's much more mature and much more focused than I would say at the point he was at a year ago, when I was coaching him with the second team. I'm really proud of him, the way that he's been able to put focus on the day-to-day and the game-to-game," Richter mentioned. "Because I think of a lot of things, positive and negative, that happened to him this year. Having a great experience in Denmark, but it didn't start out perfect, and he earned his way in. When he came back here, he earned the starting spot. A couple months later called for the national team for his first caps to the national team. Comes back and is able to right away again put his full attention back in with the team and play a couple of good games after that. Um, so overall, his maturity in dealing with the things that are going on around him, I think, has been really impressive.".

Pierre credits his family and the team for helping him stay grounded through what has been an absolute whirlwind year. Next up is a trip to USMNT camp before helping anchor the defense for the club as they face the Newly introduced England Revolution in the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs. Plenty for a young player to juggle, but after the year Pierre has had, this will feel more normal than what he has already accomplished.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adriano Galliani reveals who convinced him to run for FIGC President and assures he will ‘absolutely’ stick with Italy coach Roberto Mancini if replacing Giovanni Malagò.

The Italian Football Federation was thrown into chaos last month when it was ruled that Malagò did not have the requisite paperwork when he first ran for President, so his June landslide election was null and void.

Faced with the need to put the FIGC under a Special Commissioner until the next election on December 14, the CONI (Italian Olympic Committee) decided to give the role to Malagò.

At the time, it was assumed this would be just a stopgap solution until he could be elected properly, but former Milan and Monza CEO Galliani threw his hat into the ring.

“There are two candidates, the vote is in four weeks, so we’ll see what happens,” Galliani told Sky Sport Italia.

“I was convinced by some phone calls from clubs, but also from the Players’ Association and Coaches’ Association. I had noted no in the past, but (Coaches’ Association President) Renzo Ulivieri told me that the rapport with the Lega Calcio was at its best when I was President. Umberto Calcagno told me the same thing.

“I have a very long and detailed proposal for my tenure, which I have already presented and deposited.”.

There was the risk of further chaos when Galliani’s lawyer had presented an appeal against Malagò running for FIGC President again, because there was confusion over who had the right to propose him from Genoa.

However, that was dropped just before the deadline, so the election will go ahead on December 14.

“I told my lawyer to let it go, Italian football already has so many problems,” explained Galliani.

“I spent 50 years in Italian football, there are too many things to sort out, and I wrote them all in my initiative.”.

The major decision made by Malagò as FIGC President was to appoint Mancini as the Italy coach, so is that something Galliani would confirm if he won the election?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, real Betis needed a stoppage-time equaliser and extra time to beat Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey round of 128. Manuel Pellegrini's weakened side avoided an upset and now await the second-round draw.

Real Betis came from behind late on to beat Navalcarnero in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Thursday 12 November. Riquelme settled the tie in extra time at Santo Domingo. Manuel Pellegrini’s side finished with ten men after Aitor Ruibal was sent off.

Recent findings suggest that the venue carried history for the Betis coach. Santo Domingo is where Pellegrini, then in charge of Real Madrid, suffered the 2009 cup defeat known as the ‘Alcorconazo’, El Gol Digital noted. Navalcarnero, founded in 1953, play in Group V of Segunda Federación. The club moved the tie away from its own Municipal Mariano González ground. It chose Santo Domingo, which holds roughly 5,000, to make room for its more than 2,000 members. The club stated money was not the only reason.

Recent findings suggest that riquelme opened the scoring in the fifth minute from a Ruibal assist, and Betis led at half-time. Álvaro Leis equalised in the 49th minute from a free-kick routine set up by Navalcarnero’s coach. Leis then turned provider for K. Vazquez, who put the hosts ahead in the 79th minute.

Marina levelled in stoppage time, with Ruibal credited with the assist. Riquelme’s second goal came in the 96th minute. Diego Llorente went off in extra time after a heavy blow to the head. Isco missed a penalty in the 117th minute. Already booked in the 90+4th minute, Ruibal received a second yellow and a red card in the 118th. Navalcarnero felt they should have had a penalty for a challenge by Pablo Fornals, and the tie was played without VAR, Infobae (EFE) reported.

The figures show how much Betis dominated. They had 73% of the ball, took 29 shots to Navalcarnero’s 12 and won 13 corners to 3. They completed 864 accurate passes. Dani Ceballos earned a 9.2 rating with 3 key passes. On the same night, Levante also needed extra time in the first round, winning 2-1 away to CD Tarancón.

Betis were without several regulars. Valles, Marc Roca, Abde, Parrott, Deossa and four other players were away on international duty. Cucho Hernández was injured. Betis agreed the new date after talks with the RFEF and Navalcarnero, knowing that any players called up by their national teams would miss the match.

The win follows a 2-0 victory over Elche. For Navalcarnero, the defeat ended a run of five matches without loss, including a 3-2 win over Numancia. They host Getafe II in Segunda División RFEF on Sunday 15 November. Betis visit Sevilla in LaLiga on Saturday 21 November.

Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.

Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.

That came despite his incredible impact in the second half of last season when he replaced Ruben Amorim and led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League.

And on Saturday night, a few days after his tenure ended, Carrick attended a tour date of The Courteeners.

According to the band's schedule, they were performing at Alexandra Palace in London.

One fan shared a photo on X from the gig, with the caption 'One hell of a day out'.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend.

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

According to recent reports, some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

Following his sacking on Thursday after ten months in charge, Carrick issued a heartfelt statement reflecting on his tenure.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’.

Carrick was relieved of his duties at Man United on Thursday after a dismal start to the season.

The axe ultimately fell on Carrick on Thursday, yet the writing was on the wall for several days beforehand as speculation spread and United's hierarchy worked towards an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino.

Many former United stars were hugely critical of their former club, with Gary Neville calling their treatment of Carrick 'disgusting', while Peter Schmeichel labelled it 'very disrespectful'.

Rio Ferdinand also compared United's 142-word statement announcing his sacking to 'like ChatGPT' after there was no comment added by club chiefs.

United are back in action on Sunday when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool in what will be Pochettino's first game in charge.

City begin proceedings in 12th after victories over Porto and AEK sandwiching that rip-roaring 4-2 defeat by the champions PSG at the Etihad.

City, who seemed in rude health after seven successive wins at the start of the Premier League campaign despite the guilty verdicts in the Premier League’s case against them for financial cheating, have wobbled since then, losing their last two league games. Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma are both suffering bouts of poor form, other individual errors continue to plague them and, although they are creating hatfuls of chances, they have been thwarted by a combination of imprecise finishing and the excellence of Zion Suzuki and Bart Verbruggen.

It has been revealed that for all their travails on the road – RB Leipzig have also lost at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich – they have won all their home Bundesliga matches as well as a 1-0 victory over PSV in this competition. Their total of 22 league goals is second only to Bayern’s 27 and Antonio Nusa, a Norway team-mate of Erling Haaland, is in sparkling form flitting behind strikers Christopher Nkunku and Romulo. City, whose full-backs, if you can describe the centre-backs and midfielders who play either side of the centre-halves in that way, never look fit for purpose defensively and may well have their work cut out tonight if he drifts wide.

The Red Bull coaching principles, which have treated us to the dross football of Jesse Marsch, Matthias Jaissle and Ralph Hasenhüttl, all about the long pass, the central channel, counter-pressing and second balls, have a upcoming proponent in Martín Demichelis, the forner City and Argentina defender who won the title in 2014 at the Etihad. Three years ago he led River Plate to the title in Argentina, the highlight of a coaching career also spent running Bayern’s U21s, Monterey and Mallorca.

These two have met six times in the last five years, City winning four, most notably the 7-0 thrashing at the Etihad in 2023’s Round of 16, the year they went on to win the Treble. Leipzig’s only victory came at home five years ago in the sixth, redundant group game when City and PSG had already clinched qualification for the knockout stages.

Antoine Semenyo is City’s only absentee; Leipzig will have to do without one-cap Germany midfielder Assan Ouédraogo and former Chelsea striker Marc Guiu.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gotham FC will play Sunday's NWSL semifinal against the Kansas City Current at Icahn Stadium over concerns about the quality of the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, which was described as "atrocious" during the team's quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign.
  • Industry observers note that the NWSL Shield winners announced the venue shift on Monday, less than a week before the semifinal.
  • The quarterfinal match, though, was marred by complaints about the playing surface from both teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gotham FC will play Sunday's NWSL semifinal against the Kansas City Current at Icahn Stadium over concerns about the quality of the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, which was described as "atrocious" during the team's quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign.

Industry observers note that the NWSL Shield winners announced the venue shift on Monday, less than a week before the semifinal. Icahn Stadium is a smaller venue on Manhattan's Randall's Island that seats 5,000 and has been sparingly used by Gotham, who have played the vast majority of their home games at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, N.J. since 2021. Sports Illustrated Stadium seats 25,000 and welcomed nearly 13,000 for Sunday's 1-0 win over the Reign.

The quarterfinal match, though, was marred by complaints about the playing surface from both teams. Reign head coach Laura Harvey described the field as "shit" in a post-match interview with ESPN, while captain Jess Fishlock called it "atrocious." Gotham head coach Juan Carlos Amoros also apologized for the quality of the surface after the NWSL fined the club $10,000 in the build-up to the quarterfinal match.

Industry observers note that "We as a team worked extremely hard to earn a home playoff berth," captain Tierna Davidson said in a statement on Monday. "What we got was a field that is not the standard this club, this league, or our fans deserve. The quality of the game is not up for debate, so we've made the difficult decision to move to Icahn Stadium on Sunday. A smaller stadium means many of you will not be there, and that is the hardest part of this decision. You have turned every ground where we have played into home, and that does not change on Sunday. We have never needed a perfect setting to make a place ours. Bring everything you have on Sunday, and we will leave it all on the field.".

The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium appeared to show the wear and tear from recent events, not least of which was Gotham's regular season slate. Gotham are the secondary tenants at the venue, which is owned by Fresh Jersey's Hudson County but counts MLS' Red Bull New York as the primary tenants and operators of the facility. The stadium was also the site of a rugby doubleheader the weekend before Gotham's quarterfinal against the Reign, which led Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell to describe the surface as "sandy" and "unstable.".

In a recent development, the Red Bulls will still play a friendly on Saturday at Sports Illustrated Stadium against Club America. The friendly will take place during the men's international break, so several first-team players will miss the match, which will serve as the final game of their season since they missed out on the MLS Cup playoffs for a second season in a row.

Industry observers note that "We wish Gotham FC the best of luck in their semifinal at Icahn Stadium," Red Bull New York told CBS Sports in a statement. "We look forward to our match on Saturday at Sports Illustrated Stadium.".

It has been revealed that gotham have staged two games at Icahn Stadium in the last year and change – a Concacaf W Champions Cup group stage match in 2025 and their 3-2 win over the Reign in July. There is the perception of convenience for the club's fans based in the city of Newly introduced York, who would otherwise have to trek to New Jersey to attend a game. As far as public transportation goes, though, Icahn Stadium is only accessible via the M35 bus; a footbridge connecting Randall's Island to 125th Street is also an option, as is driving to the stadium.

It has been revealed that "It's nice for folks who live in Upcoming York to have a somewhat closer venue," Jen Muller, a longtime member of the official Gotham supporters group Cloud 9, told CBS Sports last year. "I know it's not ideal for a lot of them, too, because there's one bus that comes here, but you adapt.".

The pitch at Icahn Stadium, which has also hosted New York City FC II matches this year, is not expected to be an issue and was not during the Concacaf match in 2025.

"I don't really want to talk too much about it, but the Sports Illustrated Stadium has traditionally been the best pitch in the league," Amoros noted at the time, "and the last couple of games, it's definitely been far away from that, so this pitch here is outstanding.".

Industry observers note that gotham's move to Icahn comes despite the fact that they avoided a scheduling conflict with Sunday's results. The NWSL's broadcast slots for this year's semifinals were Saturday at 12 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+ and Sunday at 3 p.m. ET on ABC; the Washington Spirit will host the Utah Royals on Saturday, while Gotham will take on the Current on Sunday.

For Gotham, the Sunday time slot was the preferred option because of a pre-existing scheduling conflict with the Red Bulls' Saturday friendly against Club America. They had to wait out the result of the Spirit's quarterfinal with the Portland Thorns, though, since the Thorns would have been unable to host a semifinal at 9 a.m. local time. Gotham seemed destined to return to Sports Illustrated Stadium once they avoided the scheduling conflict but the quality of the pitch caused newly introduced concerns.

It has been revealed that the Spirit, meanwhile, avoided a scheduling conflict of their own. They were originally set to host the Royals at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the NFL's Washington Commanders, because their usual venue of Audi Field was instead hosting Secretaries' Cup, a Division III college football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy. The college football game has since been pushed to a later slot that day, Spirit CEO Kim Stone crediting Audi Field owners D.C. United and sponsor Lafayette Federal Credit Union for underwriting "the additional costs necessary to bring this semifinal match home.".

In a recent development, the challenges stem from the fact that many NWSL teams are secondary tenants in their home stadiums, the Spirit included – MLS' D.C. United own and operate Audi Field. Some, like the Royals and the Orlando Pride, benefit from sharing ownership groups with MLS clubs, while the Current own and operate CPKC Stadium. The rest often rent the local MLS team's stadium, Gotham and the Spirit included, but it creates other unique conflicts for teams with more control over their venues. The Current's quarterfinal against Angel City on Saturday, for example, kicked off at 11 a.m. local time in order to fit the broadcast slot on CBS.

According to recent reports, celta Vigo were rarely troubled in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Friday 13 November. Jutglà struck twice before the half-hour mark, and Swedberg added a late double after Salamanca UDS had gone down to ten men.

The Galician side were 3-0 up at the break at Villares de la Reina. They finished with goals from three different players and assists from five team-mates, against a Salamanca side coached by Jorge García.

Industry observers note that jutglà opened the scoring in the 15th minute, converting an assist from Milla. Eight minutes later he struck again, this time set up by Febas, to put Celta firmly in control.

Opara was also booked for Salamanca in the 89th minute as the hosts saw out the closing stages.

The result echoes the previous meeting between the clubs in this competition. Celta won 7-0 in Salamanca on 3 December 2024.

Elia Caprile has been the most effective goalkeeper in Serie A this season at Cagliari, but reveals Antonio Conte ‘did not take it well’ when he left Napoli, is open to playing for Albania, and nearly gave up his career.

The 25-year-old has kept four clean sheets in 11 Serie A games so far this season, more than any other goalkeeper in the division, and also made more saves than anyone else.

Despite that, he knows that he’s very far behind in the ranking for Italy, where Gianluigi Donnarumma, Guglielmo Vicario, Marco Carnesecchi and Alex Meret are all ahead of him.

“I would love to silence all those who wouldn’t bet a cent on me when I was little, that fire inside me is still burning,” Caprile told the Corriere della Sera newspaper.

“I thought of quitting so many times, especially when a few coaches were mean to me. I wasn’t playing, I was shorter than the other kids, I was fat.

Recent findings suggest that “I was made to feel bad about it and lost my way, but I got advice from two goalkeeping coaches Bressan and Squizzi at the moment I needed them the most. They highlighted me football is made of sacrifice, both before and after training.”.

Caprile has never played for Italy at senior level, and now has Albanian citizenship thanks to his partner.

“I don’t know if something can come from it, so far no Federation has knocked at my door. If they do, then I will evaluate.”.

He already made the decision to walk away from Napoli in 2025 when frustrated at the lack of playing time, and took the opportunity to shine at Cagliari.

According to recent reports, “Conte told me to stay and fight for my place with Meret, so he was honest, and so was I. He chose Alex and won the Scudetto, so it was wise, but I was 23 and really wanted to play. I felt the physical need to be on the pitch,” explained Caprile.

It has been revealed that “So in January, I told him I wanted to leave. Conte did not take it well, but he understood.”.

#1411. Bundesliga treat Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or as beacon of hope as Germany's competitiveness questions linger

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2115 w)
📖 Baca

Bundesliga treat Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or as beacon of hope as Germany's competitiveness questions linger

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2115 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that even if the hints of a smile never fully leave his face, there is an overriding sense of practicality when Philipp Lahm speaks.
  • Industry observers note that "It helped Harry Kane and Michael Olise that they came from another country," Lahm mentioned four days after Kane's substantial win.
  • Recent findings suggest that A quick glance at the data would confirm the hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that even if the hints of a smile never fully leave his face, there is an overriding sense of practicality when Philipp Lahm speaks. He seems to have shed the intensity associated with the life of a professional athlete nearly a decade after retiring, but the characteristics of a World Cup-winning captain are hard to miss. He is friendly and open but also serious, so when the topic of conversation shifts to Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph, he is politely unflinching in his assessment of what the award means for soccer in Germany.

Industry observers note that "It helped Harry Kane and Michael Olise that they came from another country," Lahm mentioned four days after Kane's substantial win. "I think it's quite difficult for a German player playing in the Bundesliga [to win the Ballon d'Or].".

Recent findings suggest that A quick glance at the data would confirm the hypothesis. The last Bundesliga-based player and the last German player to win the sport's most prestigious individual award was Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer in 1996. A German player has only finished inside the top three of the Ballon d'Or three times since, the last being Manuel Neuer in 2014, while Kane is only the seventh Bundesliga player to rank in the top three since Sammer's win. Lahm seamlessly links the pattern to another less-than-ideal trend in Germany's top flight -- Bayern Munich, with whom he won eight Bundesliga titles, are the division's indisputable kings.

Sources indicate that they have lost the title just once since the 2012-13 season, a lack of competitiveness at the top of the table a natural consequence of their dominance. This is, in some ways, not Bayern's problem, but a narrative persists in Germany regardless. Players have historically been unable to reach the peaks of the game in Germany because of the circumstances, inspiring a wide-ranging set of side effects. Kane's move to Bayern was not designed to be anything other than the right move at the right time for a player talented enough to compete for the UEFA Champions League, but three years later, those invested in the Bundesliga's success are beginning to treat him as a beacon of hope.

"I do hope that the good players stay in the Bundesliga," Lahm noted, "so I'm hopeful through Harry Kane that a lot of other players will follow because it's possible to win and play here.".

In a recent development, the argument to join Bayern Munich is a straightforward one, if you ask sporting director Christoph Freund -- "you can win titles with us," both in Germany and Europe. Bayern have won the Champions League twice in the last 14 years, a feat matched only by Paris Saint-Germain and topped by Real Madrid. The Bundesliga's distribution of wealth favors them in this case, to the point that it likely played a sizable role in signing Kane and Olise. The balance of financial power in the European club game, though, has shifted as Bayern re-established their foothold in Germany -- the Premier League has become the sport's league of choice because it has the financial might to back up the claim. Players like Robert Lewandowski and Mario Gotze used to prove their worth at other German clubs (and in their specific case, Borussia Dortmund) before climbing up the food chain and joining Bayern. Florian Wirtz's jump from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool in 2025, though, is an example of a latest world order, one some hope Kane's Ballon d'Or might change.

Sources indicate that "It's all about the attention, so when you're successful with the German national team that's visible, but then when you play also successful soccer with Liverpool, then the attention in U.K. is much bigger," Lahm stated, citing Wirtz's hypothetical Ballon d'Or case as an example, "so that would be more difficult for a German player in the Bundesliga alone, rather than changing to somewhere else outside and being successful abroad.".

The Bundesliga's international appeal has not only taken a hit on the sporting side in recent years. Bayern's executives believe their club makes up around 50% of the league's brand value globally, and though they are unapologetic about their strengths on the pitch, they also argue they are doing too much of the heavy lifting. Rouven Kasper, a member of Bayern's executive board, pointed to Premier League clubs' oversized presence on preseason tours as a primary example for the Bundesliga to follow but all but questioned the league's interest in the strategy.

It has been revealed that "The league needs to be, as well, stronger and bring more reach, but the league exists from the clubs," Kasper noted. "We are the spearhead of German football, and I think together with the other clubs and together with the league, we need to be even more active in the markets ... it's not enough, and at the end, it's about people, community. We want to be approachable. We want to talk to the people. We want to be there, as the Bundesliga and Bayern alone cannot do it together with Dortmund, so we need more activities from the league and being in different markets, as the U.K. guys are doing and also the Spanish guys are doing. We will do our part.".

Their part includes potentially using Kane as a hook for player recruitment, even if other leagues have their charms for the world's top talents.

"I think everybody knows the Premier League is the biggest league at the moment," Freund said. "Also, Spain is really attractive with Real Madrid and Barcelona, but we know we are Bayern Munich and the German Bundesliga is also really a strong league, a really good league, outstanding stadiums, outstanding atmosphere, and you can [perform] also on a very high level like Harry, the next step in his career, and therefore, I think Bayern Munich and also the German Bundesliga is very attractive, also, for international top players.".

Some in the Bundesliga, though, are resigned to the fact that there are certain things Bayern -- and other European clubs -- will simply beat them to. Dortmund have held strong in their attempts to mount a title challenge this season, level on points with Bayern after eight games thanks to Saturday's 2-2 draw in Der Klassiker. For the foreseeable future, though, recruitment of elite talents cannot and will not play a central role in their quest to win silverware. "We never refuse, or we never avoid to tell you guys where we are from, but in comparison to Munich, Madrid, London, Paris, Milan, we are from Dortmund and from a purely economic perspective, we are far behind them," Borussia Dortmund CEO Carsten Cramer mentioned. "If they [are] just interested in trophies and silver, if they look for the Ballon d'Or player wearing a black and yellow shirt, maybe that is something we can't offer to them.".

While Bayern's brand is wrapped in the quiet luxury of their domestic stronghold, Cramer argued that Dortmund's appeal is a qualitative one.

In a recent development, "In the last 13 years, we didn't become champion but though we didn't become champion, the interest in Dortmund is still increasing and the amount of people following our club on social media and wherever we travel in the world is quite huge," he said. "We are able to offer a different approach: closeness. That is the Dortmund way, and I think that is maybe one of the reasons that many, many hardcore supporters of one club do have a sympathy for us as a second-love club, which I do not complain about, and that is our way. I don't want to make us too small by saying we are a niche club, but we are for sure a bit different, and I don't complain about [it].".

Industry observers note that patrick Owomoyela, a defender for Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund team that won back-to-back Bundesliga titles more than a decade ago, can clearly map out the recipe to beat Bayern to the top. Strong squad composition and compatibility go a long way, and he believes the current iteration of Dortmund has that -- he praised head coach Niko Kovac's defensive structure and commended him for "sprinkling the creativity" into the team in the months since taking the job in January 2025. There is just one problem, though.

It has been revealed that "Even though you know the recipe, the soup is not always the same," he noted. "Even though you put in the same ingredients, it's not always tasting the same, and if it does, maybe it's not the perfect soup, you know? So you need to find that special something.".

Much like Cramer, Owomoyela has a qualitative argument of his own to make when it comes to breaking Bayern's decades-long dominance in the Bundesliga. The "special something" for his Dortmund team was a sense of camaraderie, the foundation of which was Klopp's joyous approach, though he openly admitted that is a difficult thing to replicate.

"This is sometimes the mentality of the guys or the personality of the guys and how that fits together, on top of the stuff that they can do with the ball and as I said, we weren't the best in terms of playing football," he said. "We were the best team. We had the most fun. We really liked doing a lot of stuff together. We were like a family, and you don't find that all the time, and it gets harder, I would say, every year because football has changed. The plans of players nowadays are totally different ... These guys have a plan, so they want to be part of something for this period of time, but then they want to move on, and that makes it, of course, hard to find that chemistry because he is gone next year.".

It is the issue he identified with Leverkusen, the Bundesliga's last champion not named Bayern. Their rise up the ranks in the 2023-24 season was ambitious and impressive, but two years later, the mainstays of their title-winning campaign were elsewhere. Wirtz left for Liverpool, as did Jeremie Frimpong, Granit Xhaka now finds himself at Sunderland, Piero Hincapie now plays for Arsenal and then-head coach Xabi Alonso made a stop at Real Madrid before landing at his current post at Chelsea. Jonathan Tah, meanwhile, went the old-school route and now plays at Bayern. The next challenger to Bayern's throne will likely face the same fate for the foreseeable future, no matter whether its stars move to Munich or settle in England.

Saturday's draw between Bayern and Dortmund, though, has offered a flicker of optimism that the Bundesliga might have a title race on its hands before the next great team gets stripped for parts. The 2-2 scoreline flatters Dortmund -- Bayern racked up 4.48 expected goals and were unlucky when the crossbar denied them on both Kane's second-half penalty and a late strike from Lennart Karl, while the visitors generated just 0.74 xG. Owomoyela argued, though, that Bayern have their flaws.

"What's it gonna take to take that away from Bayern after all these years again?" he asked. "It's just to believe that it's possible and I think the Bayern team showed in this season as well, or especially maybe, that you can wound them, you can hurt them and something is possible. You can see that in almost every game they played, even in that cup game [against second-division side Magdeburg on Oct. 28] that they just had and they won it 6-1 ... They hit the post, hit the crossbar, scored a goal, had two other big chances so now take a team with more quality, with the right kind of belief, there might be something possible.".

Industry observers note that saturday's Klassiker only added to the Bundesliga's week of good news, presenting a different case of the league's strengths than Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph, one that will likely take precedence in the short term. The longer Dortmund keep pace with Bayern, the more intriguing the Bundesliga becomes, and at this stage of the season, the possibility of a genuine title race is easy enough to dream up. That sense of optimism, though, tends to give way to the league's current realities. Even if Dortmund answered the question in the affirmative once, there's a long way to go until anyone can definitively say that Bayern can be topped.

"We weren't really eye-level competitors," Owomoyela remarked about Dortmund's ability to compete with Bayern in the years since their back-to-back Bundesliga titles. "We were there and we were able to hunt, but from a little distance, and I think everybody understands that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The patterns of the international match calendar are well known at this point. Players pack their suitcases, board planes, spend a small stretch of days with their compatriots … and in the U.S. men's national team's case, answer questions about their coach landing a upcoming job.

Industry observers note that from the moment Mauricio Pochettino walked into a midtown Manhattan auditorium two years ago to make his opening remarks as the USMNT head coach, his presence has felt temporary to many. It was not just because job security is an increasingly unrealistic concept for soccer coaches, nor was it only down to the fact that Pochettino initially signed a deal that would expire 22 months later. The last two years have been full of reminders that the USMNT job is one of several that could be available to him – he has openly talked about wanting to return to the Premier League, did not deny that his representatives may have met with AC Milan in the weeks before the World Cup and regularly talks about his undying love for Tottenham Hotspur. The latest iteration of a years-long pattern came Tuesday, when reports out of England suggested Pochettino was a top contender for the Manchester United gig, which is not vacant yet but will be once the club finally parts ways with Michael Carrick.

Sources indicate that the cadence is unusual, since coaches rarely invite reasonable questions about seeking employment elsewhere. At this stage of Pochettino's tenure with the U.S. team, though, it would be difficult to characterize it as a surprise. It would be equally hard to argue that the pattern does not come with the territory, defender Antonee Robinson acknowledging as much hours after the news broke.

According to recent reports, call it What You Want: A weekly podcast where Jimmy Conrad, Charlie Davies and Tony Meola cover all things USMNT and the state of the beautiful game in the United States. Catch the show YouTube live every Tuesday and Friday at 10 a.m. ET.

In a recent development, "That news kind of got sprung on us, like the rest of the world, I'd say," he said. "Similar things happened in the past, happened at the World Cup where huge teams lose their manager and they start looking at possible candidates and for us to have a manager who's linked with those sorts of jobs means we're very lucky to work with a top-level manager but it never seems to leak into the work we do, whether it's the World Cup or whether it's going to be this camp.".

Pochettino's wantaway pattern may be annoying but it reflects the overarching sentiment of his tenure with the USMNT thus far. He is easily the highest-profile coach to take the job and U.S. Soccer is well aware of that. It is why they lined up donors to secure his signature two years ago to make him the federation's highest-paid coach ever, and why there is reportedly a $10 million buyout clause in the new deal he signed after the World Cup. For the first time in the program's modern history, they hired a coach with genuine international appeal. Even if Robinson should instead spend his time talking about the upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, the fact that Pochettino would be courted by others was baked into his appeal.

It has been revealed that "Even when we first met a couple summers ago, there were lots of other people interested in having Mauricio and team join," U.S. Soccer CEO J.T. Batson noted in May as chatter around the Milan job took center stage in the early days of the USMNT's World Cup preparations. "He had standing offers from other places to come. He wanted to be here. He's a substantial believer in what we're doing at U.S. Soccer. He's a big believer in soccer in America and he's a big believer in this men's team and so, throughout this entire process, when you have top-class talent, whether it's salespeople, whether it's marketing people or whether it's coaches, other organizations want them and throughout this, Mauricio and team have been incredibly transparent. They've been great partners and are, of course, excited about the summer … There's been a longer list of outreach than what has even been reported and so they've been great about that.".

The key difference here is that he reportedly might be interested in United's offer, according to the Guardian, but the situation remains the same, despite the timing being strange, three months after agreeing a four-year deal. If Pochettino does not end up on United's touchline, his time with the USMNT was never destined to last forever, and U.S. Soccer admitted to it months ago.

According to recent reports, "We actually, on a monthly basis, have a succession planning session for all of our coaches across all of our teams and so as a part of that, we have intends for renewals," Batson mentioned on that May day. "We have plans for interims and we have plans for replacements because you never know what's going to happen. It's a global sport, lots going on and so that's a standard part of us growing up as U.S. Soccer.".

Many might spend the subsequent weeks after Pochettino's hypothetical departure questioning Batson's claim that the Argentine is actually a "big believer in soccer in America," though the argument is irrelevant as far as the USMNT goes. Pochettino's hire, along with that of U.S. women's national team head coach Emma Hayes a year earlier, was a large statement of intent from U.S. Soccer's leaders like Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, who are relatively new to their jobs. Pochettino's exit, therefore, would raise the question of how they continue that vision two years later, especially after outlining an ambitious path for the men's program in the coming years.

High-profile candidates like Pochettino are not exactly easy to come by, as the initial effort to hire him demonstrated. Ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola is easily the most notable name on the market but it is entirely unclear what his next coaching move might be, even if that should not discourage U.S. Soccer from reaching out if they have a vacancy. The options thin out from there if they are only to be measured on their flair, though, making it hard to envision a perfect follow-up act to Pochettino in the short term.

There is a theory that U.S. Soccer may be resigned to picking from a locally sourced talent pool, something that is reinforced by a suggestion that Pochettino was a false steward of American soccer. His departure, if it comes in the short term, is not actually an indictment on U.S. Soccer's approach, nor should it encourage the federation to go for the safest pick next. Pochettino's tenure, at least up until this point, has been an example in reaping rewards for a bold strategy, one that should continue long after he is gone.

According to recent reports, pochettino's time with the USMNT has so far been characterized by mixed results, including some low lows that he bears just as much responsibility for as his players. It is not hard to see why he was a good fit for the job, though, and it is not because he makes headlines – his high-intensity, attack-minded style of play actually suited the player pool. The fact that he has coached in a UEFA Champions League final and won a Ligue 1 title with Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar may help with player buy-in, but it would not have papered over the cracks if his version of the USMNT was not actually a decent marriage between his tactical preferences and the players' natural skillsets.

He continues to feel like a good fit in the post-World Cup months, especially as he oversees a generational shift in the player pool. Pochettino's tenure at Spurs, where he initially made a name for himself as a coach, was defined by his trust in young players but as it pertains to the USMNT's up-and-comers specifically, they already seem well-positioned to slot into his tactical set-up. The team's next great prospects are almost all exclusively attackers; Neil Pierre, the Philadelphia Union 19-year-old in the midst of a breakout season, is so far one of the few notable exceptions at center back.

It has been revealed that A quote-unquote big name might not be a realistic option for the USMNT if Pochettino leaves now, though he may have theoretically made the gig more attractive to prospective coaches. More importantly, though, U.S. Soccer is now well-positioned to make a hire based on style and specifically an entertaining and effective style that captured the attention of an otherwise uninterested nation during the World Cup. Straying from that, no matter if Pochettino's successor is world renowned or otherwise, would not match the potential of the USMNT's rising stars, nor would it align with U.S. Soccer's own vision.

#1403. Tech Report: What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?
